definition.def: Modern means relating to the present time, for example the present decade or present century.
examples: ...the problem of materialism in modern society.
It's the sort of thing that would be very difficult to prove in any modern court of law.

definition.def: Something that is modern is new and involves the latest ideas or equipment.
examples: Modern technology has opened our eyes to many things.
In many ways, it was a very modern school for its time.
As the country's economy prospered, it was bound to want a modern army.

definition.def: People are sometimes described as modern when they have opinions or ways of behaviour that have not yet been accepted by most people in a society.
examples: They were very modern Tories in almost every sense.
She is very modern in outlook.

definition.def: Modern is used to describe styles of art, dance, music, and architecture that have developed in recent times, in contrast to classical styles.

examples.sentence: But the origins of what is now generally known as modern architecture can be traced back to the social and technological changes of the 18th and 19th centuries.
By the 1980s the coexistence of different styles of architecture in the same building became known as Post Modern.
It is one manifestation of how work and leisure are organised as separate and regulated spheres of social practice in modern societies.

Indeed acting as a tourist is one of the defining characteristics of being 'modern' and the popular concept of tourism is that it is organised within particular places and occurs for regularised periods of time.

A substantial proportion of the population of modern societies engages in such tourist practices new socialised forms of provision have developed in order to cope with the mass character of the gazes of tourists as opposed to the individual character of travel.
It has been said that to be a tourist is one of the characteristics of the modern experience.
Travel is a marker of status in modern societies and is also thought to be necessary for good health.
Although modern information technologies can reduce the demand for physical transport by facilitating teleworking and teleservices, the requirement for transport continues to increase.

Modern science - linguistic, archaeological and genetic evidence - has definitively proved the moai builders were Polynesians, but not how they moved their creations.
